Engineer / Technical Officer - Road Design (East)
Department of Transport and Planning
Apply now Applications close Tuesday 6 October 2026 at 11.59pm
Overview
Work Type: Ongoing - Full-time
Salary: $81,496 - $98,955
Grade: VPS 3
Occupation: Engineering
Location: Melbourne - Eastern suburbs
Reference: 12067
About Us
We create thriving places and connected communities. We plan, build and maintain Victoria’s transport, planning and land services. We are committed to a safe, inclusive and high-performing workplace.
We welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds and are committed to creating a safe, inclusive workplace where our people can thrive and do meaningful work.
About the role
The Engineer / Technical Officer Road Design supports the design, documentation and delivery of road and traffic engineering projects across Victoria. Working under supervision, the role contributes to projects from concept through to detailed design, including road layouts, intersections, drainage, safety barriers, signage, line marking and 3D modelling.
The role uses MicroStation and OpenRoads to develop designs, drawings and project documentation within agreed timeframes and budgets. It applies road design and traffic engineering standards and supports Safe Systems principles to improve road safety. The role also builds effective stakeholder relationships and prepares reports, briefs and technical advice.
What   we’re   looking for   (Selection Criteria)
You’re someone who:
You’re someone who works collaboratively, sharing information, supporting colleagues and contributing positively to achieving team goals.
You’re someone who delivers work effectively, prioritising tasks according to urgency and impact, working to agreed plans and maintaining accurate project records.
You’re someone who applies sound judgement and problem-solving skills, using established policies and processes to resolve issues and seeking guidance when needed.
You’re someone who applies foundational engineering knowledge professionally, using relevant standards, guidelines, codes and risk controls to develop and document practical engineering solutions.
You’re someone who is adaptable and technically capable, open to new approaches and developing skills in road and traffic engineering, roadside safety, and CAD tools including MicroStation and OpenRoads.
Click   here   to access the Position Description.
Qualifications and experience
You’ll bring:
Victorian Driver’s License
Construction Induction Card (White Card)
Ability to travel within the state for site inspections
Pre-employment checks and employment conditions
Relevant pre-employment screening and reference checks will be required.
Applicants must be an Australian Citizen, Permanent Resident or hold a valid work permit or visa necessary for the nature of the position.
Recipients of Victorian Public Service (VPS) voluntary departure packages should note that re-employment restrictions apply.
How to apply
Click the ‘Apply’ button to be redirected to our recruitment platform, where you may need to create an account to submit your application.
Applications close at 11.59pm on Tuesday,  6 October 2026.
Please include both your resume and a cover letter addressing how your experience addresses each of the key selection criteria for the role. All applications must be submitted via the online portal, we’re unable to accept email or manual submissions.
For further information about the role, please contact Vincent Nguyen, Senior Manager Road Design at vincent.nguyen@transport.vic.gov.au.
Redeployees
If you are a VPS redeployee, please state this in your cover letter and include your case manager’s contact details. This helps ensure your redeployment status is appropriately considered. For more information on redeployment, visit the Victorian Government policy.
Important Information
If you require any adjustments to fully participate in the recruitment process or need the advert or attachments in an accessible format (e.g., large print), please contact us. We're here to support you.

About the Department of Transport and Planning
We create thriving places and connected communities. We bring together transport, planning, land use,
precinct and policy functions in a single department to deliver the best outcomes for Victorians.
Together with our portfolio agencies, we are responsible for planning, building, operating and maintaining
Victoria’s transport, planning and land services for use by all.
We foster a safe, inclusive and constructive place to work.

About the group
Network Design and Integration delivers transport priorities through the planning, development and
maintenance of an integrated pipeline of projects and strategic initiatives that provide safe, efficient and
sustainable outcomes to all Victorians.
Assets and Engineering Division (A&E) enables a safe, resilient and fit-for-purpose Victorian transport system
through whole of lifecycle decisions based on systematic and disciplined technical excellence. A&E influence
each stage of the Victorian transport asset lifecycle to realise a reliable transport network for our
communities, through policy, planning, investment and technical standards.
Our work optimises the value and sustainability of allocated resources (capital and operating) across the
Victorian transport portfolio and its asset base
We’re focused on outcomes that deliver more choice, connections and confidence in our travel, ensuring the
whole transport network works as one to deliver better services and outcomes.
Design Services is a multidiscipline design branch within A&E that provides expert quality technical advice
and design services for our clients across the Department, including expertise in geotechnical, pavement,
structural and road design.

 About this position
Position purpose and context

The Engineer / Technical Officer Road Design sits within Design Services branch and is responsible for the
design, documentation and delivery of road design and traffic engineering projects within DTP’s pipeline of
work under sound supervision as assigned by Team Leader Road Design.

The role’s responsibility will include, under sound supervision, the design development of projects at all
stages, from conceptual design, through to full detailed design and plan production, and provision of advice
and review for the whole of the life of the project.

Tasks will involve design development of intersection functional layouts, horizontal and vertical geometric
design of roadways, design of roadside infrastructure such as safety barrier, drainage design and
modifications to existing networks, signage and linemarking, sign face design, development of 3D models for
construction purposes, quantity extraction, drawing production and associated documentation and
reporting. Design development tasks are facilitated using Bentley Systems MicroStation and OpenRoads
platforms under sound supervision within agreed timeframes and budgets.

Embedded into our work is the ongoing commitment to Safe Systems principles, providing a safe road
network for Victorians.

Position accountabilities
– Accountability 1 - Road Design and Traffic Engineering Delivery: Utilises foundational working knowledge
  of road design and traffic engineering frameworks, policies, standards and guidelines to develop, design
  and document road design and traffic engineering projects in both the Victorian rural and urban road
  environments, under sound supervision within agreed timeframes and budgets.
– Accountability 2 - Stakeholder Management: Develops and maintains effective relationships with peers
  and customers across DTP, as required, and understands and addresses stakeholder issues under sound
  supervision.
– Accountability 3 - Communication: Prepare reports, briefs and correspondence on complex issues that
  impact at project level. Convey specialist concepts and advice in alignment with design guidelines under
  sound supervision.
– In line with Section 31A of the Public Administration Act 2004 (Vic) other duties may be assigned consistent
  with employment classification, skills, and capabilities.

Key selection criteria

Core Victorian Public Service (VPS) capabilities
– Core VPS Capability 1 - Working Collaboratively (Foundational) - Cooperates and works well with others in
  pursuit of team goals; Share information and acknowledge others’ efforts; Step in to help others where
  required
– Core VPS Capability 2 - Project Delivery (Foundational) – Executes work tasks against plan; where plans
  are not defined, prioritises tasks in line with the urgency and impact of tasks; Utilises approved task
  management tools; Maintains accurate project records.
– Core VPS Capability 3 - Critical Thinking and Problem Solving (Foundational) - Seeks resolution of
  problems through policy or process guidelines; Otherwise seeks guidance by providing information and

   ideas relevant towards resolution of problem. Understands concepts enabling improvements in critical
  thinking and problem solving.
– Core VPS Capability 4 - Professional Knowledge (Foundational) - Displays a theory-based knowledge of
  the fundamentals of engineering disciplines. Identifies and describes the basic principles pertinent to a
  specific area of engineering practice and context. Analyses data to systematically design engineering
  solutions to address a well-defined problem. Adheres to engineering professional, workplace and statutory
  controls, policies and codes for ethics, compliance and risk. Creates and maintains documentation and
  data associated with a small-scale engineering project.
– Core VPS Capability 5 - Flexibility and Adaptability (Foundational) – Considers the merits of new ideas
  and approaches. Is willing to develop and apply new skills.



Technical capabilities
– DTP Technical Capability 1 - Geometric Road Design and Documentation (Foundational): Incorporating
  functional road and traffic engineering design. Has a foundational level of understanding of the road and
  traffic engineering design standards and guidelines. Can apply this understanding in the design and
  documentation of road design and traffic engineering to suit site-specific constraints and environment.
– DTP Technical Capability 2 - Roadside and Ancillary Elements Design (Foundational): Incorporating barrier
  design and roadside safety. Has a foundational level of understanding of the roadside infrastructure
  design policies, standards and guidelines and can integrate this into the overall road design.
– DTP Technical Capability 3 - Cadd Skills (Foundational): Incorporating 2D layouts, 3D modelling and plan
  production. Has a foundational level of understanding and application in the use of Bentley Systems
  MicroStation and OpenRoads platforms to undertake road design tasks. May also have a working
  knowledge of other programs such as CaddPro, AutoTurn and GuideSign.

Qualifications and Experience
– Relevant tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering (mandatory)
– Knowledge of road design, roadside infrastructure and drainage, applying relevant standards and
  guidelines such as Austroads Guide to Road Design, relevant DTP Supplements and other relevant
  guidelines in relation to road design in both rural and urban road environments (desirable)
– Experience in the use of Bentley Software, including MicroStation Connect, OpenRoads Designer and
  Projectwise (desirable)

Other position-specific requirements
– Victorian Driver’s License
– Construction Induction Card (White Card)
– Ability to travel within the state for site inspections

Ordinary hours of work
Ordinary hours of work are Monday to Friday between 7:00am and 7:00pm.
